```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Many breeding pipelines export genotype data as a wide CSV: rows are
samples, columns are markers, cells are short genotype tokens
(`A`/`H`/`B`, `0`/`1`/`2`, `AA`/`AB`/`BB`, ...).

`csv_to_vcf()` converts these to a valid VCF v4.2 file. It runs
[`validate_genotype_table()`] and [`validate_marker_map()`] internally
and aggregates all errors into the returned `beagler_result` — no VCF is
written if anything fails.

## Inputs

```{r}
library(beagler)

csv_path <- system.file("extdata", "tiny.csv", package = "beagler")
map_path <- system.file("extdata", "tiny_map.tsv", package = "beagler")

read.csv(csv_path)[1:3, 1:6]
read.delim(map_path)[1:3, ]
```

## Convert

```{r}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
result <- csv_to_vcf(csv_path, map_path, out)

result$ok
result$summary$inferred_encoding
result$summary$n_samples
result$summary$n_markers
```

The output VCF passes M5's Beagle-target validation:

```{r}
validate_vcf(out, target = "beagle")$ok
```

## A peek at the body

```{r}
cat(readLines(out)[6:10], sep = "\n")
```

## Failure mode: no partial output

If validation fails — duplicate samples, invalid alleles, encoding
mismatch — `csv_to_vcf()` returns errors and writes nothing.

```{r}
bad_csv <- data.frame(
  sample_id = c("s1", "s1", "s2"),
  rs1 = c("A", "B", "H"),
  rs2 = c("H", "A", "B")
)
bad_map <- data.frame(
  marker_id = c("rs1", "rs2"),
  chrom = c("chr1", "chr1"),
  pos = c(100, 200),
  ref = c("A", "C"),
  alt = c("T", "G")
)

bad_out <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
result <- csv_to_vcf(bad_csv, bad_map, bad_out, sample_col = "sample_id")
result$ok
result$errors$code
file.exists(bad_out)
```

## Encoding overrides

`encoding = "auto"` (the default) detects the encoding from the data.
You can override and the validator will reject any token that doesn't
fit the chosen alphabet:

```{r}
result <- csv_to_vcf(csv_path, map_path, tempfile(fileext = ".vcf"),
                    encoding = "AHB")
result$ok
```

For the AHB encoding, the convention `ahb_ref = "A"` (default) means
`A` codes homo-REF and `B` codes homo-ALT. Pass `ahb_ref = "B"` to swap.
